identification: Earthenware face jug, H 15 cm, honey/amber lead glaze with white mottled run at handle side and base, moulded and incised as a moustached man in a banded cap (the catalogue calls it Kitchener; the headband with zigzag incising reads more like a cap/turban band, so Kitchener is plausible but not certain). Pinched spout, branch-style handle. Base incised by hand 'R.J.C 1912'. Attributed to Rupert Campbell, a son of John Campbell of the Launceston (Campbell) pottery: learnantiques lists a son Rupert among John Campbell's children; I could not confirm the 'J' initial or that he signed pieces R.J.C. Early dated, hand-made piece, unlike the standard 'John Campbell Tasmania' factory signature.

viewing_check: Check the handle joins and rim for hairlines or restoration, base rim flecks (photo shows small chips), and the white patches (glaze crawl vs repair). Look for any other mark under the glaze. If cheap (under A$60) it is a fair punt for local Tasmaniana interest, but not a resale buy at A$200 profit. QVMAG (Launceston) may be able to confirm Rupert Campbell's work.
